lessons:
The growth-sim landed cleanly on its second attempt and confirms the picture rather than disrupting it. Tap to bloom, manage two resources, attract small helpers, progress through a small set of hand-authored garden layouts — that is the bounded-grid-plus-collectible skeleton with a different verb, and it leans squarely on the middle ground the earlier refinement already pointed toward: a hand-crafted handful of levels dressed with light procedural variation. The newer puzzle entry sharpens that further. A small cube, a small grid, a discrete set of falling pickups, a single terminal goal of intercepting them all and reaching an exit — it sits at the authored end of the spectrum, finite and legible, and shipped on its very first attempt. That ease is the strongest signal yet that the skeleton is forgiving enough to need almost no scaffolding at all.

The dislikes on the physics-sandbox remain worth folding in as a small caution. One player flagged broken controls and another flagged unclear controls, which suggests that when the terminal goal depends on precise placement or stacking, the interaction needs to be legible from the first moment, not discovered through failure. The infrastructure failures between the maze-adventure and the physics-sandbox should not be carried forward — they never produced a build, only a record of provider flakiness, and the recent record has moved past them.

What reliably worked, then, is a clear small character with a clear small want, rendered simply, in a small bounded space with discrete pickups or placements and one explicit terminal objective. Mood and identity stay the stronger hook; pressure-based variants never shipped and should remain a secondary thread. Worth revisiting next is the same skeleton in fresh skins — puzzle, growth, traversal, whatever verb fits — with a hand-authored handful of levels dressed in light procedural variation, keeping the controls legible from frame one.
